proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Deduce the injectivity of part one from the injectivity of base change for cycles over fields discussed in the relative fields section, then for part two work with the coefficients of the pulled back families as integer-valued functions on the points of transdegree r, define the base change operation on such functions by the multiplicity formula whose coefficients are positive integers by the multiplicities lemma, use associativity of base change in the explicit form of the displayed multiplicity identity, invoke the coequalizer lemma together with the footnote construction to obtain a unique rational-valued function alpha with g^*alpha = alpha', and conclude integrality of alpha at each point by choosing a preimage point with separable residue field extension where the multiplicity is one because the fibre is reduced (source lines 847-918)

standard_prerequisites.name: Injectivity of base change for cycles over fields: for a locally algebraic scheme X over a field k, the base change map Z_r(X) to Z_r(X_{k'}) on r-cycles is always injective (relative-cycles chapter, Section section-relative-fields, canonical tag 0H4E)
standard_prerequisites.use: Yields part (1): the base change map on families of r-cycles over X/S is injective whenever S' to S is surjective.

standard_prerequisites.name: Positivity of multiplicities in field extensions: the multiplicity m_{Z', Z_K} of an irreducible component Z' of the base change of an integral locally algebraic k-scheme Z by a field extension K/k is one or a power of the characteristic of k, in particular a positive integer (relative-cycles chapter, Lemma lemma-multiplicities-field-extension, canonical tag 0H4F)
standard_prerequisites.use: The coefficients m(x', g) in the base change operation on coefficient functions are positive integers.

standard_prerequisites.name: Existence and coequalizer property of lifts of points of transdegree r under a surjective base change: every x of transdegree r admits a lift x' of transdegree r, and any two such lifts are both projections of a common x'' of transdegree r in the double base change (relative-cycles chapter, Lemma lemma-coequalizer-dim-r, canonical tag 0H4W)
standard_prerequisites.use: Together with the displayed multiplicity identity and the footnote construction, gives a unique rational-valued function alpha with g^*alpha = alpha'.

core_obligations: Prove the two descent statements (proof lines 847-918). For part (1), invoke the injectivity of the base change map on cycles over fields discussed in section-relative-fields (tag 0H4E); the argument works as long as S' to S is surjective (proof lines 848-850). For part (2), denote alpha'' = pr_1^*alpha' = pr_2^*alpha' the common value and identify the families with their coefficient functions on the sets of points of transdegree r (proof lines 852-863); define the base change operation g^* on such functions by (g^*varphi)(x') = m(x', g) varphi(x), where m(x', g) is the multiplicity of the irreducible component Z' with generic point x' in the fibre Z_{s'}, always a positive integer by lemma-multiplicities-field-extension (tag 0H4F), and define pr_1^* and pr_2^* on coefficient functions analogously (proof lines 864-888); associativity of base change gives pr_1^* composed with g^* equals pr_2^* composed with g^*, which the author marks small detail omitted and then makes explicit as the identity m(x'', pr_1) m(pr_1(x''), g) = m(x'', pr_2) m(pr_2(x''), g) for x'' whose projections have transdegree r (proof lines 889-898); by lemma-coequalizer-dim-r (tag 0H4W) and the elementary footnote construction setting alpha(x) = alpha'(x')/m(x', g) for a lift x' of x, well defined thanks to the displayed identity, there exists a unique map alpha from (X/S)^{(r)} to the rationals with g^*alpha = alpha' (proof lines 899-908); it remains to show alpha takes integer values, the author noting one needs to see that alpha determines a locally finite sum on each fibre, which follows from the corresponding fact for alpha' (small detail with its content supplied in the same parenthesis, proof lines 909-911); finally, given x of transdegree r with image s, pick s' over s with separable residue field extension kappa(s')/kappa(s) (exists by hypothesis), choose x' of transdegree r over x, and observe m(x', g) = 1 because the fibre Z_{s'} is reduced in the separable case, whence alpha(x) = alpha'(x') is an integer (proof lines 912-917).
proof_roadmap: Part (1): deduce injectivity of the base change map on families of r-cycles from the injectivity of base change over fields (proof lines 848-850).

Part (2) setup: take coefficients, view the families as functions on points of transdegree r, and define the base change operation by the multiplicity formula with coefficients m(x', g) positive integers (proof lines 852-888).

Associativity of base change gives the explicit multiplicity identity; with the coequalizer lemma and the footnote construction obtain a unique rational-valued alpha with g^*alpha = alpha' (proof lines 889-908).

Integrality: at each x choose a preimage point with separable residue field extension, where the multiplicity is one because the fibre is reduced, so alpha(x) = alpha'(x') is an integer (proof lines 909-917).
